I've been farming these 12 mu for 25 years now, since I was 23. My father taught me the basics and the rest I learned by doing — good years, bad years, droughts, floods, you name it. I finished middle school, so I can read the leaflets the extension office hands out, but honestly I always adjust their numbers based on what I see in my own fields and what my neighbors are doing.

This year money is a bit tight because my daughter's school fees went up, and while my son sends some money back from his factory job in Shijiazhuang, I don't want to keep asking him for more. So I have to watch every yuan. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves — our son is in the city and our daughter is in school, so it's just the two of us for daily labor. For cotton picking in the fall I'll need to hire some women from the village; I can't handle 8 mu of cotton alone.

I put about 8 mu in cotton — that's my cash crop, what pays the bills. The other 4 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer. That way we have flour and grain at home, and if prices are decent I can sell a bit. 

For the wheat — I planted it last October with saved seed from the year before, like always. It came up okay. Now it's early spring and I need to decide on the green-up fertilizer. The extension guy said I should topdress 15 kg of urea per mu, but last year I put down about 12 kg and still got around 400 kg per mu, which was plenty for our needs. I'll do about 12 kg again this year — save a bit of money and the wheat looks healthy enough. I'll irrigate twice if it stays dry: once at jointing and once at grain filling. Pumping water costs about 30 to 40 yuan each time, so I'll watch the sky. One spray for weeds and maybe one for disease if the weather turns damp.

For maize — I'll plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is tight, only about a week, so I use minimal tillage. I buy hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 15 kg worth, then topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high. If the summer is wet I might not irrigate at all, but usually I need one good watering when the tassels come out. I'll spray herbicide once — the weeds grow fast in summer.

For cotton — this is where I put my money and attention. I plant in mid-to-late April using an improved variety. I plow the field once with my small tractor and prepare flat beds. Base fertilizer is important: I spread about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. Then at squaring I topdress with urea, about 8 kg per mu, and again at flowering another 8 kg. Total nitrogen ends up around 16 or 17 kg per mu. The extension people say I could go higher, but I can't afford more and this level has worked for me. I irrigate twice — once at flowering, once at boll filling. The well water isn't free; the electricity for the pump adds up fast. For pests, I watch carefully. If I see aphids or bollworms I spray. Usually I need two or three sprays total, plus herbicide at the start. For yield, I expect about 250 to 280 kg of lint per mu if the weather cooperates. I'm not expecting a bumper year — just a normal one. I'd rather be conservative than disappointed.

Total costs will run around 5,800 yuan, maybe a bit more. That's most of my cash. But if the cotton does okay, I should clear enough to get through the winter and pay for my daughter's school.
